subject: Private deployment - DPA/KMS responsibilities and operator access boundaries
messages:
From: Charlotte Li <charlotte.li@meditech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Barnes <lbarnes@meditech.com>, Meditech Legal <legal@meditech.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment for pilot - DPA and KMS Qs

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security and legal teams asked me to pull a few items together so we can scope the procurement paperwork for the pilot (private deployment into our VPC). Can you confirm the following points and point me to any template language you prefer?

1) Customer-managed keys: we want BYOK with key material generated and controlled by Meditech KMS (AWS KMS). Can Redwood support an external KMS endpoint and confirm there is no backup export of key material from the private deployment?

2) Operator access and maintenance: we need a concrete description of what remote maintenance looks like. Can you provide the minimum operator privileges required, and whether any maintenance requires cross-connect breaks or a temporary tunnel?

3) Subprocessors list and notifications: please send the current list of subprocessors that would touch telemetry, crash logs, or managed artifacts in the private package. We will need 30 days' notice for any additions per our policy.

4) International transfers: a portion of our logs may cross into EU support queues. If we keep the private deployment in our US region, what guarantees can you provide about log routing and persistent storage locations?

I've attached our initial DPA redline and a CSV with a short vendor inventory for your reference. Legal would like a short addendum template for data transfer safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) if needed.

Can we set a short call next week with Ben and Monica on your side?

Thanks,

Charlotte Li
Security Program Manager
Meditech

[attachment: MED-DPA-redline-20261001.pdf]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Charlotte Li <charlotte.li@meditech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment for pilot - DPA and KMS Qs

Charlotte —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up-front, followed by some detail below. Happy to walk through on a call. Proposed slots: Tue 10/6 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 10/7 09:00–09:30 PT — let me know what works.

Summary answers:
- BYOK: supported. We can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/CloudHSM) via a customer-managed key endpoint. Redwood does not store unencrypted key material in our control plane.
- Operator maintenance: our operator model for private deploys is "no default network egress" — maintenance is performed via a customer-controlled maintenance gateway (temporary SSH/HTTPS tunnel initiated by the customer) or on-site runbook if preferred. Operator actions requiring elevated access are gated by break-glass with time-limited one-time credentials and recorded in an immutable audit trail.
- Subprocessors: attached is a redacted subprocessors CSV (telemetry, monitoring agent vendors, kernel patch providers). We will email 30 days' notice for additions and can negotiate narrower scopes on a per-deal basis.
- International transfers: logs and persistent storage remain in the region you provision; ephemeral telemetry for support may transit into our support tooling in the US only if you opt into remote log shipping. We can offer a no-remote-log option where all support traces remain in-customer VPC and are accessed only via secure screen-share / in-person review.

Details / suggested DPA language:
- KMS integration: propose simple clause: "Customer retains sole control of key material. Redwood's control plane receives only key handles and performs cryptographic operations via the customer's KMS endpoints; Redwood does not export or escrow key material except as required by court order under a mutually agreed process."

- Operator access boundary: we suggest defining three personas in the DPA/SoW: Operator (maintenance engineer), Support Analyst (support-level diagnostics with RBAC-limited visibility), and Customer Admin. For private deploys: Operator privileges are limited to ephemeral diagnostic sessions; permanent privileged credentials are never stored in the deployment. Any operator session must be initiated through customer gateway and produce a signed audit record.

- Subprocessors: we'll provide a deal-specific subprocessor schedule and accept a 30-day notification clause. For any subprocessor that would host customer content outside the provisioned VPC, we agree to additional contractual guarantees (DPA appendix + SOC/ISO attestation).

Next steps: Ben / Monica, can you prepare a one-page addendum (data-transfer/SCCs) and a short operator-access paragraph we can send to Meditech? I can take point on the DPA redline.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment for pilot - DPA and KMS Qs

Ben / Monica —

Forwarding Meditech's asks. Quick negotiation playbook below (feel free to edit):

1) BYOK: concede support for AWS KMS integration but hold firm on "no-export" language. Offer optional key-escrow for production only with strict legal process and split-escrow (custodian + Redwood) if they require escrow for operational continuity.
2) Operator access: default is customer-initiated maintenance gateway. If they insist on remote maintenance, require a scoped SOW with break-glass controls, time-limited credentials, and a signed attestation each time.
3) Subprocessors: provide redacted list and propose a 30-day notice + opt-out if a new subprocessor would materially change processing.
4) Data transfers: offer two flavors — (A) No-remote-log (all telemetry stored in-customer) or (B) Remote-support with auditably redacted traces. Attach a one-page SCC-addendum draft for option B.

Can you have a draft operator paragraph + SCC addendum by EOD Monday? I will review the DPA redline and propose inline language for section 5 (Data Transfers) and section 9 (Access & Maintenance).

Thanks,

Steph
